Q: Why do the apps written in java run only on android, even if java is platform independent A:

Java itself is platform-independent, but that does not mean every Java application can run on every device.

Java sources are converted into bytes, which require a runtime environment compatible with Java (JVM or an equivalent JVM-compatible runtime) to run.

Android Applications are particular case

Android apps are mostly developed using Java (or Kotlin), however they cannot run on the traditional Java Virtual Machine (JVM).

However, Android compiles Java bytecode into DEX (Dalvik Executable) format that runs on the Android Runtime (ART) (formerly Dalvik).

Android also comes with the company's very own SDK and APIs that differ from the Java SE standard Java SE libraries.

This is because:

Desktop Java application developed with Java SE is not able to be run straight on Android.

Additionally, the Android APK is not compatible with Windows, macOS, or Linux as these operating systems do not have an Android Runtime as well as the Android framework.

The statement "Write Once, Run Anywhere" is only valid if the platform of choice has the compatible Java runtime. Platform independence means that the same Java code can be run on a variety of operating systems as long as they are running a JVM that is compatible. However, it doesn't mean that apps designed to run on one platform (such like Android) will work on every platform.

In simple terms:

  • Java is a platform-independent language.

  • Applications are dependent on platforms because they are dependent on runtimes that are specific to the platform and libraries.

  • Android applications require Android Runtime (ART) along with Android APIs. Therefore, they can only be used on Android devices, but not on all systems that support Java.

Q: Using VSCode and getting NoClassDefFoundError A:

If none of the other options posted here work, try locating your java install. If it was altered after VSCode was installed, VSCode may be trying to locate java somewhere other than where it is.

After locating, delete the jdk folder and reinstall java. VSCode should now be functional.

Q: Conditional statement for insert, update or delete A:

Well, the OPEN..FETCH..LOOP has become pretty old-fashioned. You should simply use single insert/update/delete statement based on the parameter. It is going to be far more efficient than your looping constructs.

CREATE OR replace PROCEDURE sp_cs (p_var txt.col1%TYPE) 
IS 
BEGIN 
    CASE p_var 
      WHEN 'I' THEN 
        INSERT INTO main_tbl 
        SELECT * 
        FROM   txt; 
      WHEN 'D' THEN 
        DELETE FROM main_tbl m 
        WHERE  EXISTS (SELECT 1 
                       FROM   txt t 
                       WHERE  m.col2 = t.col2); 
      WHEN 'U' THEN 
        UPDATE main_tbl m 
        SET    m.col2 = (SELECT v_rc.col2 
                         FROM   txt 
                         WHERE  m.somecol = t.somecol); -- the column you want to compare while updating
    END CASE; 
END; 

/

While It is not clear from your update query what you are trying to achieve, I assume you have a common column in txt while updating col2 from main_tbl. Moreover, I have used your parameter as a procedure argument p_var. You may use it as local variable if you don't want to pass it.

Q: Case expression instead of multiple selects A:

You can use CASE expressions with the SUM() function, as follows:

SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN lcs.statename = 'Follow Up' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  as [Name 1],
       SUM(CASE WHEN lcs.statename = 'Initial Review' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  as [Name 2],
       SUM(CASE WHEN lcs.statename = 'Execution' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  as [Name 3],
       SUM(CASE WHEN lcs.statename = 'Holdback' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  as [Name 4]
FROM hsi.itemlc as ilc
LEFT JOIN hsi.lcstate as lcs on lcs.statenum = ilc.statenum
WHERE lcnum = '412'
  AND status = '0'

Which result in conditional counts of each state name.
